stem.en: Two particles are prepared in a definite, pure, entangled joint quantum state. What can be said about the state of just one of the particles, considered on its own?
stem.et: Kaks osakest valmistatakse ette kindlas, puhtas, põimunud ühises kvantolekus. Mida saab öelda ühe osakese oleku kohta, vaadelduna eraldi?

label.en: That one particle, considered alone, is in a mixed state, even though the full two-particle system remains in a well-defined pure state.
label.et: See üks osake, eraldi vaadelduna, on segaolekus, kuigi kogu kaheosakeseline süsteem jääb hästimääratud puhtasse olekusse.

label.en: That particle must have a completely certain, definite value for every observable, since the joint state is pure.
label.et: Sellel osakesel peab olema iga vaadeldava jaoks täiesti kindel, määratud väärtus, kuna ühine olek on puhas.

label.en: The question doesn't really make sense — 'mixed state' is just another name for the same superposition the joint system is already in.
label.et: Küsimusel pole tegelikult mõtet — 'segaolek' on lihtsalt teine nimi samale superpositsioonile, milles ühine süsteem juba on.

label.en: That one particle must also be in its own pure state, since a pure joint state can only be built from individually pure single-particle states.
label.et: See üks osake peab samuti olema oma puhtas olekus, kuna puhast ühist olekut saab ehitada ainult individuaalselt puhastest üheosakeseolekutest.
